headline: Former ASP arrested over enforced disappearance of Sayeedi witness
summary: Fazlur Rahman was detained by DB police in Dhaka for his alleged role in the 2012 abduction of Sukhranjan Bali from the International Crimes Tribunal.
details: Detectives have arrested a former assistant superintendent of police (ASP) over allegations of involvement in the 2012 'enforced disappearance' of Sukhranjan Bali.
Bali, a resident of Pirojpur, had gone to the International Crimes Tribunal to testify in the defence of Jamaat leader Delwar Hossain Sayeedi.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam confirmed that Fazlur Rahman was arrested from his home in Dhaka on Thursday night.
On November 5, 2012, Bali went missing from the tribunal premises after arriving to testify. The incident drew significant national and international attention at the time.
While law enforcement agencies later claimed Bali had been found near the border, his family and human rights groups alleged he had been abducted from the tribunal compound.
The DB has not yet disclosed the specific charges that will be brought against Fazlur Rahman or whether other individuals were involved in the abduction.
caption:
A former ASP has been arrested for the 2012 'enforced disappearance' of a witness in the Sayeedi trial.

Detectives have arrested a former assistant superintendent of police (ASP) over allegations of involvement in the 2012 'enforced disappearance' of Sukhranjan Bali.

Bali, a resident of Pirojpur, had gone to the International Crimes Tribunal to testify in the defence of Jamaat leader Delwar Hossain Sayeedi.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam confirmed that Fazlur Rahman was arrested from his home in Dhaka on Thursday night.

On November 5, 2012, Bali went missing from the tribunal premises after arriving to testify. The incident drew significant national and international attention at the time.

While law enforcement agencies later claimed Bali had been found near the border, his family and human rights groups alleged he had been abducted from the tribunal compound.

The DB has not yet disclosed the specific charges that will be brought against Fazlur Rahman or whether other individuals were involved in the abduction.

Source: Somoy News, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: Scaloni dismisses [[FIFA favoritism claims against Argentina]] as social media rumors
headline: Scaloni dismisses FIFA favoritism claims against Argentina as social media rumors
summary: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni says the team ignores baseless social media rumors regarding special treatment from FIFA.
details: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has spoken out against rumors of FIFA favoritism toward his team, dismissing them as baseless social media chatter.
During a press conference in Miami, Scaloni emphasized that the best way to handle such claims is to simply ignore them and avoid reading social media posts.
He noted that in the era of likes and retweets, unfounded rumors can easily be amplified and distorted to hide the actual reality of the situation.
Scaloni warned that anyone can post baseless claims that can go viral in a second, and stated that the team does not give these narratives any importance.
The coach's remarks came ahead of Argentina's match against Cape Verde in the final round of 32 in the World Cup.
He concluded by stating that while social media has its benefits, it also has a negative side where nonsense can spread instantly across the globe.
caption:
Does FIFA give Argentina special treatment? Coach Lionel Scaloni has a clear answer for the social media rumors.

Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has spoken out against rumors of FIFA favoritism toward his team, dismissing them as baseless social media chatter.

During a press conference in Miami, Scaloni emphasized that the best way to handle such claims is to simply ignore them and avoid reading social media posts.

He noted that in the era of likes and retweets, unfounded rumors can easily be amplified and distorted to hide the actual reality of the situation.

Scaloni warned that anyone can post baseless claims that can go viral in a second, and stated that the team does not give these narratives any importance.

The coach's remarks came ahead of Argentina's match against Cape Verde in the final round of 32 in the World Cup.

He concluded by stating that while social media has its benefits, it also has a negative side where nonsense can spread instantly across the globe.

#Argentina #LionelScaloni #FIFA #WorldCup #FootballNews

Source: Prothom Alo, Somoy News
